guideline: WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use, 5th Edition (2015, updated 2016)

mec_categories.1: No restriction — method can be used without restriction
mec_categories.2: Advantages generally outweigh risks — method can generally be used
mec_categories.3: Risks generally outweigh advantages — method not recommended unless no alternatives available
mec_categories.4: Unacceptable health risk — method must not be used

rules.notes: Combined hormonal contraceptives contraindicated in breastfeeding women <6 weeks postpartum (infant exposure to oestrogen)
Progestogen-only pill: generally safe but monitor infant
Injectable progestogen: generally safe but trace exposure; monitor infant
Injectable progestogen SC: generally safe but trace exposure; monitor infant
Progestogen implant: generally safe; trace exposure; monitor infant
LNG-IUD: trace progestogen; generally safe in breastfeeding
Copper IUD: non-hormonal; safe in breastfeeding
COC in breastfeeding 6 weeks–6 months: oestrogen may reduce milk supply. Use alternatives where possible.
Severe hypertension (systolic ≥160 mmHg): COC contraindicated — cardiovascular risk
Progestogen-only pill generally acceptable in hypertension
DMPA in severe hypertension: risks may outweigh benefits; consider alternatives
DMPA-SC in severe hypertension: risks may outweigh benefits
Migraine with aura: COC contraindicated — significantly increased stroke risk
History of DVT or PE: COC contraindicated — high VTE recurrence risk
Progestogen-only pill: generally acceptable after DVT/PE
DMPA: generally acceptable after DVT/PE
Progestogen implant: generally acceptable after DVT/PE
Copper IUD: non-hormonal, no VTE risk
Current or past breast cancer: all hormonal methods contraindicated
Current or past breast cancer: progestogen-only pill contraindicated
Current or past breast cancer: DMPA contraindicated
Current or past breast cancer: DMPA-SC contraindicated
Current or past breast cancer: progestogen implant contraindicated
Current or past breast cancer: LNG-IUD contraindicated
Active/severe liver disease: COC contraindicated — hepatic metabolism impaired
Active liver disease: progestogen-only pill generally not recommended
Active liver disease: implant risks may outweigh benefits
LNG-IUD: mostly local effect; generally acceptable in liver disease
Copper IUD: non-hormonal; safe in liver disease
Smoking ≥35 years: COC contraindicated — high cardiovascular risk
Progestogen-only pill: safe in older smokers
ARVs (EFV, NVP, ritonavir-boosted PIs) reduce COC efficacy via CYP450 induction; COC unreliable — use alternatives
ARVs (EFV, NVP, PIs) may reduce POP efficacy; use DMPA, implant, or IUD instead
Implant efficacy may be reduced by EFV/NVP-based ARV regimens; advise of small residual risk
Copper IUD in adolescents: generally acceptable; counsel on insertion discomfort and expulsion risk
LNG-IUD in adolescents: generally acceptable; counsel appropriately
COC use ≥40 years: generally acceptable if no cardiovascular risk factors; use with caution
